video_title: Talking Knicks' back-to-back wins in Toronto with Justin Termine | The Putback with Ian Begley

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on the Knicks' early season offensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: Nobody can shoot the ball here early on in the season.
quotes.quote: The offense has not been the same. Nobody can shoot the ball here early on in the season. You have three of the major guys under 40 percent right now with Mikal Bridges, who it is nice to see him get a little confidence the last two games defensively in the overtime win over Toronto last night. He gives you the 17 points, seven of 11, hit a big three late, so hopefully that gets him going. Josh Hart has not got going yet. They have to put him on the bench the last couple of games, so he has not been shooting the ball well. And OG Anunoby is under 40 percent for the season, at least heading into last night. And then Jalen Brunson has been around 43 percent. Even though Brunson continues to hit big shots, really the only guys a part of the regular rotation that have upped it and shot better this year are Karl-Anthony Towns, probably not taking enough shots, and he has been one of the better players in the league so far, and then Landry Shamet, who has stepped up and played a huge role.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on why Karl-Anthony Towns deserves MVP consideration
quotes.excerpt: He is leading the league right now in rebounding. He is rebounding the ball well.
quotes.quote: I do not know if he would get MVP votes because you have to go Luka, Wembanyama, probably Jayson Tatum, Cade Cunningham. After that, maybe we could finagle a vote or two. Stephen Curry would have been up there if he was not hurt, but he has been absolutely spectacular so far, Karl-Anthony Towns. He is shooting the ball efficiently when they run the offense through him. Last night, I think he had the eight assists. He is leading the league right now in rebounding. He is rebounding the ball well. And that is a part people get on his defense. He was great defensively last year in the postseason, and also rebounding is a part of defense because you are ending a possession. He has got to get credit for that. So he is rebounding the ball well, he is, I think, leading the NBA as of last night in true shooting percentage, so he has been efficient.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine argues the Knicks should pay Karl-Anthony Towns now
quotes.excerpt: You have to pay him right now and then if it is proven you cannot win, you could offload him.
quotes.quote: What Boston did, and that is where I am, is they paid Jalen Brunson before they even won, and then they decided, all right, we are going to pay him because we have to, or else we cannot win. And then afterwards, down the road, once it was proven, hey, this has run its course, we cannot win anymore like this, we have been eliminated in the second round, in the first round, then we offload the contract. And they gave Jalen Brunson 300 plus million dollars, and I think Karl-Anthony Towns is a better player. I think what you need to do is pay him right now and then if it is proven like in the next couple of years you cannot win, you could offload him, even if not return is awesome, which I think a lot of people think the return for Jalen Brunson was not awesome or as good as it could have been. So that is what I think you need to do right now with Karl-Anthony Towns.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on why the Knicks shouldn't trade OG Anunoby
quotes.excerpt: I do not think you can trade your second best player.
quotes.quote: I do not think you can trade your second best player, and I think OG Anunoby, you know, had a case for that throughout the playoffs last year as the second best player. But I do not think you can make a, you know, you can blow it up and not give the opportunity to repeat, right? I think the last time that we saw that was 2011 where Dallas lets go of some guys because they wanted to reboot and go out and get Dwight Howard and Darren Williams, and then they were just never the same. And with OG Anunoby, it is like a lot to ask him to sacrifice the money and his touches and his role. Right with Brunson, you are asking him just to sacrifice his money, right, initially, and I am sure they are going to pay him on the next contract. But he is sacrificing one thing. He is just sacrificing his money. OG Anunoby is sacrificing his money and his role.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on Mikal Bridges' slow start and why he shouldn't be benched
quotes.excerpt: You do not go full in and bench him because you are going to need him in order to win the championship.
quotes.quote: The question popped up at the outset was, what do you do? Do you bench him? And Mike Brown took some of his minutes, but you do not go full in and bench him because you are going to need him in order to win the championship. So like, all right, maybe he is not playing well right now, but you stick with it, you deal with maybe some regular season losses just to keep his confidence up, because the the weird part is how slow he started off. You would think like he would head into this season with a ton of confidence, all of these guys, but he was averaging 15 points per game on almost 60 percent shooting the last 14 or 15 playoff games after he got hot in game six against Atlanta, and he used that that blowout where he went off to kind of turn himself into a really big, not just defensive piece, but offensive piece.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on OG Anunoby's role and potential
quotes.excerpt: I feel like OG Anunoby was just as good last year at times as Jalen Brunson was.
quotes.quote: I feel like OG Anunoby was just as good last year at times as Jalen Brunson was when he won Eastern Conference Finals MVP and Finals MVP a couple of years ago and won the championship and probably more accepting of his role as well, because I think he could play a bigger role. I mean, he could be asking for more shots per game and he kind of just fits into the offense. He is a far better defensive player than Jalen Brunson as well, and you are like kind of asking him to be your number three, right? If Brunson is your number one and Karl-Anthony Towns is your number two, you are asking him to be your number three, and Boston won a championship with Jalen Brunson as their number two.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on the surprising success of the Lakers and Grizzlies
quotes.excerpt: I had them as the six seed in the Western Conference. For them to be the one seed and to be this dominant is a little bit surprising.
quotes.quote: Philadelphia I thought would not be this good this early. I would have thought maybe they could be this in March, April, May, but the fact that they have come together this early is a little bit scary. And then I would also say that what the Lakers are doing, I mean, even Austin Reaves misses a couple of games, I had them as the six seed in the Western Conference. For them to be the one seed and to be this dominant is a little bit surprising. JJ Redick has to be in the conversation for Coach of the Year. Those are two teams that I thought would be good anyway, just was not sure it would be this soon. And then the the one team I think that has surprised everybody that I did not even have in my top 10 in the Western Conference is Memphis. And you know, you got to look at them and what Ty Jerome has done, what Buzer has done right out of the gate, they are top five I think in both offense and defense, and now they can run the system that they want because they have younger players and not have to worry about Ja Morant and and Jaren Jackson Jr., Desmond Bane, who I know they did not have last year, but they are kind of running that offense where they move the ball a lot, they got the quick like hockey rotations.

quotes.speaker: Justin Termine
quotes.summary_phrase: Justin Termine on Landry Shamet's role in the Knicks' rotation
quotes.excerpt: I think Shamet in a lot of these situations might just be the guy that he believes in to close.
quotes.quote: I think it is easy to point to the way that KAT has played, but he is an all NBA player. He has been an all star. We know he is a great player. I think mine is just kind of his Landry Shamet just part of the closing five now. Is he going to continue to close games? He can continue to be someone that is relied upon in crunch time. We are talking last year when he had a little bit of a lesser role, that has just continued to grow. He is clearly thrived. That has kind of been my biggest takeaway, that Shamet I think in a lot of these situations might just be the guy that he believes in to close and be part of that closing five. So we will keep an eye on that. But Ian, those are those are the questions we got from our lovely audience today.

quotes.speaker: Rob Dillingham
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Dillingham on his focus and growth with the Westchester Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I am really just focused on actually doing the stuff myself and getting better at the things.
quotes.quote: I really I am not really trying to show too much of anything to anyone or prove anyone. I feel like it is more of a internal and just showing myself that I can play basketball at the highest level, fit in any situation and help. So, uh, not really in details, but like overall aspect of what I feel like I could do better. I am really just focused on actually doing the stuff myself and getting better at the things so when I do get opportunity or I am actually ready and I am improved.
